headline: New moon springs load up The Race and Plum Gut for the best current window of July
subhead: Fluke are abandoning the warm bay for the inlets, bonito are creeping toward Fishers Island, and the rips are about to run harder than they have all month.
body_markdown:
Last week the Sound was still shaking off the blow that came through around the Fourth. Wind sat in the southwest for three straight days, kicked up a chop through the Gut that made boat control a chore, and pushed a layer of green water against the north shore that took the edge off the bass bite for 48 hours. It cleared by the weekend. Current through The Race stayed strong on the bigger tides — nothing new there — but the water column held together enough that eel guys working the north side eddies near Valiant Rock still connected after dark. Bay water on the western end of my beat has been running warm, pushing fluke out of the back bays and into the channels and inlets, which is exactly the pattern I'm leaning on this week.

Here's what matters: we're building toward a new moon on the 12th, and that means spring tides stacking through the weekend, peaking Friday into Monday. Checked the New London tide station — 8510560 — and the swings are getting bigger by the day, high stands lining up tighter to that afternoon window as the moon goes dark. Bigger tide range means more water moving through the pinch points. The Race and Plum Gut, already two of the meanest current funnels on the whole Sound, are going to be running harder than they have all month — we're talking 4 to 5 knots at max flow through the Race on the bigger swings. That's not a inconvenience, that's an opportunity. When current gets that strong, bass stack in the eddies and current shadows instead of fighting the main flow, and they feed hard right before and right after max current when bait gets disoriented and swept through the seams. That's your window. Fish the transition, not the peak.

Bass fishing right now is real but it's not blanket easy — you have to find the current break. I've been working the north side rip off Valiant Rock at first light and again at the top of the outgoing, drifting live eels on a fish-finder rig with just enough weight to hold bottom in 80 to 110 feet. Fish are there, mostly mid-20s to low-30s, with the occasional better one mixed in — heard of a few genuinely big fish scattered through the Sound corridor this past couple weeks, the kind of fish that make you fish an extra hour past when you should've quit. Plum Gut has been more consistent for numbers than size — daytime bucktail drift, white or chartreuse 1.5-ounce with a Gulp swimming mullet trailer, working the edges where the current slackens against the Orient side. That's also turning into a legit fluke spot right now. With the bay water pushing 78 degrees and fluke bailing out for cooler water, the outgoing tide through the Gut is stacking them against structure in 30 to 45 feet — I had a stretch last outing where three drifts in a row produced keeper-class fish on the same white bucktail-and-Gulp combo. Orient Point ocean side has been the better bet over the bay side for that reason alone.

Bluefish have been reliable but not spectacular — schoolie to mid-size blues chopping bunker pods off Orient and around the Fishers Island side of the Race, best worked with bunker spoons or a wire leader and a Hopkins on the troll during the morning outgoing. Nothing gorging yet, no true blitz, but enough consistent action that if bass go quiet you're not getting skunked.

The piece I'm watching closest is what's happening east of me. The cold wall that usually pins bonito and albies down around Block Island has broken down — Rhode Island Sound water jumped something like 10 degrees warmer than it's been, and that's widening the corridor west. Fishers Island sits right on that edge. I haven't had a confirmed bonito yet off North Dumpling or Race Rock, but the water's right and the bait's right, and if this holds through the week I expect the first fish to show there before they show anywhere else on my beat. Worth running out there with a bag of small Deadly Dicks and epoxy jigs just in case, especially on a calm morning with birds working.

For the coming week: I'd fish the transition tides at the Race and the Gut, not the max current — an hour either side of peak flow, working the eddies with eels at night and bucktails by day. If the wind stays out of the north and lets the water lay down, Friday through Sunday around that new moon spring should be the best current-driven bass window we've had since the June full moon faded. Plan B if the bass don't cooperate is easy — the fluke bite through the inlets is real right now and doesn't need perfect conditions, just clean outgoing water and a bucktail dragged slow along the bottom. Keep an eye east toward Fishers Island too. If that bonito corridor keeps widening the way it has, this could be the week eastern Sound guys get their first shot at them instead of driving to Block Island for it.
